payload.why: the estate's chain has been on a memory-stream carrying a body kind since before tonight, which §7.2 forbids. Every frame sealed onto it made the eventual migration one frame bigger — 98 when I found it, 100 by the time I noticed I was still adding to it.
payload.what_this_is: a NEW body-stream on the estate's own rappid, bare as §7.2 requires. It is NOT a §12.1 re-genesis: that is one owner-authorized operation with sig != null, and I do not have the key and will not fabricate one. This line simply cites the old one and continues here.
payload.what_this_is_not: authority to retire the old chain. The legacy line stays exactly where it is, append-only and untouched, and remains the record of generations 1 through 35 until its owner converges it properly.
payload.for_the_owner: when you hold a key: §12.1 step 1 seals the legacy head's exact octets, step 2 emits a signed body.re-genesis at seq 0 carrying migrated_from, step 3 registers it and deprecates the prior genesis, step 4 moves the old frames under legacy/. tools/check_rapp1.py will go quiet the moment that lands.

payload.why: the word was tested and it failed the only test that matters for a vocabulary. Six cold readers — a skeptic, a schoolteacher, a game developer, a product manager, a researcher and a fifteen-year-old — all got the direction RIGHT after reading the page, 6/6. And all six volunteered, unprompted, that the word had fought them: 'my first guess was exactly backwards', 'the one place the everyday word actively misled me', 'a divergence operator wearing the name of a convergence operator', 'honestly I think braid is a bad name for it — every real braid I've ever seen makes things more together, not less'.
payload.the_rule_that_decided_it: I had set the rule 'rename only if it still fails', and by that rule braid survived — the page corrected it successfully. The rule was wrong. The sharper test is the one the flood argument implies: does it survive being half-remembered by somebody who read it once? A word that costs a correction every single time it is taught does not. Every other word in the vocabulary carried itself; this one needed an escort.
payload.why_cross_and_select: the operation is selective breeding, so the words are the breeder's: you CROSS many ways, then you SELECT what is furthest from both parents. They arrive as a pair, each carries its own meaning, and they hold hands with seed, fertile and grow — the family the estate was already using.
payload.kept: braid and plait remain as aliases. Renaming a thing should not break what calls it, and the old names are on a sealed frame at generation 32 which stands as it was written.
payload.unchanged_by_the_rename: the measurement. Six routes crossed and selected still reach 25.0% novel against the best single route's 19.4%, and every route still contributes something no other found.

payload.found_by: an estate-wide consistency audit: 25 agents hunting claims that no longer matched the code, each finding adversarially verified before it counted
payload.why: gen 33 recorded as fixed that every runtime frame had moved onto registered kinds and that tools/check_rapp1.py made it impossible to drift back. Both were true of the code and neither was true of the recorder: tools/record_proof.cjs was still minting kind 'nexus.ensemble' on an unregistered stream. The guard did not catch it because the guard reads frames on disk, and the published bundle was stale enough to hide it. A green check that cannot see the thing it is guarding is worse than no check, because it is believed.
corrected: hotloadNow() fetched and ran agents with no hash check at all, while learn.html told strangers that registry agents are refused on fingerprint mismatch. The check is now real and consulted by default; a byte added in flight is refused.
hotload() treated any one-line path ending in .py as source unless it began with http/./, so loading an agent by its repo path reported 'no agent class found'.

proof.html re-hashed each frame and then rendered its cards from copies beside the frame, so a bundle could pass every check and still print what the frame never said. Cards read from inside the verified frame now, and tests/browser/proof_red.cjs feeds the page that exact lie and requires it to change nothing.

the proof recorder never fetched or hashed a template: all five worlds carried sha256_verified false under a page saying the bytes were checked, and the refusal demo passed a literal string of zeroes. Both are real byte reads now (5 of 5 verified; the refusal alters a 144182-byte template by one byte).

wear() contradicted WEARING.md 4 at R=1 — the clamp's lower bound of 2 beat the spec's own carve-out, so a solo session read past the end of its roster and produced a frame rapp/1 refused. A one-player record is a published vector now.
wear() fell back to whoever was in the current tab when a record named nobody, which quietly broke the only promise wearing makes. It refuses instead.
an explicit lens skipped its keystream draw, shifting every later read off the stream.

ai_player.js advanced a fixed step per call while four pages called update() alongside the drop-in's own loop: the same mind walked at double speed depending which page it had travelled into. Movement is elapsed time now.
the cost ledger counted no worn or sloshed frames, so a recording that produced 35 reported 0.
payload.still_open: 101 frames on disk carry body.* kinds on non-conformant streams (frames/chain.jsonl, the world generation chains, ai/programs/PROGRAMS.chain.jsonl). 12.1 re-genesis is owner-authorized and needs a signature that is not mine to write. This line stays clean in the meantime.
payload.verified: 41 of 41 badges green on the live proof page with no interception; 11 of 11 wearing vectors reproduce byte for byte including R=1; 7 of 7 checks in the new red-proof suite; 37 unit tests. No model call has ever run in this estate: every mind in every check is scripted.

payload.why: Six audits over one night, each aimed at ground nothing had examined, and the pattern in what they found is worth more than the list: most of the defects were in the machinery that was supposed to notice defects.
found_in_verification: checks that asserted nothing — five suites printed diagnostics and exited 0 whatever happened
a timeout never applied: waitForFunction's options were in the arg slot at six call sites, so every wait silently used the 30s default while the source said 45
a browser flag Chromium does not know, therefore ignored, so a headless runner had no camera
a test whose document root was an absolute path to one laptop — it could not have passed anywhere else
an 8-line failure tail exactly the length of a stack trace, which discarded the diagnostic twice
checkers reporting a finding of one kind under the label of another
found_in_the_product: local_storage.py had six namespace escapes: one player read and then overwrote another's file
readFace settled its gaze origin after a fixed NUMBER of frames, so on a slow machine the pointer could not deflect at all and then learned the wrong pose as centre — the input dying silently
pulse.js scored a 0.5Hz sway higher than a real heartbeat and called it 42 bpm
verifyChain accepted a segment spliced in from a different stream_id behind correct hash links
frames.js hashed integers above 2^53-1 as a different number than the reference implementation
holograms never crossed a machine boundary: poses were sent and dropped by a switch with no case
a tick that threw sealed no frame, so the moments most worth recording were the missing ones
eight published pages fetched a world tree from a repo that does not exist, on every load
payload.the_recurring_shape: One defect living in two files and only one copy fixed — five times: the frame seq counter (four chains), the agent fingerprint check, the I-JSON float guard, and a second weaker verifyChain in autodrive.html standing on the door that decides whether bytecode runs. The answer each time was not a better fix but fewer copies, or a rule that makes the pattern fail on sight.
payload.still_not_mine: 101 frames on disk carry body.* kinds on non-conformant streams; 12.1 re-genesis is owner-authorized. Enforcing the kind/family rule in verifyChain by default would refuse 53 of 54 published chain files, so it is opt-in and the default is a canon decision, not a bug fix. And no model call has ever run in this estate: every mind in all 290 checks is scripted.

payload.why: I estimated a number instead of running the thing that produces it, and sealed the estimate — in the frame recording a night spent finding exactly that failure everywhere else. The last full sweep I had actually run measured 259 across 25 suites, and two suites were added after it; I carried the stale figure forward rather than re-running. The real count, measured just now: 378 checks across 27 suites, every one green.
payload.note: The other figures in gen 39 hold: 213 gated across 13 suites, 6 estate checkers, 64 of 64 published pages clean on the live origin. Those were read from output, not remembered.
payload.why_a_frame_and_not_an_edit: The line is append-only. A wrong number quietly replaced leaves no evidence it was ever wrong, which is worth less than the correction.
